journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.angle: A deep-sea fish with a glowing lure, used to attract prey.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.barre: A deep-sea fish with a transparent head, letting it see far above it.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.betta: A small freshwater fish, known for its flowing fins, territorial behaviour, and beautiful colors.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.blobf: A deep-sea fish with a soft gelatinous body, adapted to survive under immense pressure.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.blowf: A type of pufferfish, known for making intricate designs in the sandy seabed.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.boxfi: A small box-shaped fish, capable of releasing powerful toxins when stressed.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.carp: A hardy freshwater fish, can be bred to produce koi and goldfish.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.cichl: A freshwater fish, popular in aquariums for its intelligence and striking patterns.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.clown: A brightly colored reef fish, often found living in anemones, and popularized by a children's movie.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.coela: A deep-sea fish once thought to be extinct, now considered a living fossil.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.damse: An extremely common reef fish, found in a variety of shapes and colors, often swimming in large schools.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.danio: The Danio, a small, colorful freshwater fish known for its active swimming behavior and popularity in home aquariums.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.discu: A disc-shaped freshwater fish, known for being territorial and having colorful scales.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.drago: A deep-sea fish with a long glowing lure extending from its jaw, used to attract prey.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.flash: A nocturnal deep-sea fish with glowing organs beneath its eyes, used for communication and attracting prey.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.flyin: An open-ocean fish capable of gliding above the water using its enlarged fins.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.golde: A large freshwater predator, known for its strong scales and large teeth.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.goldf: A domesticated freshwater fish bred from carp, known for its bright colors and many varieties.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.goura: A small freshwater fish, known for being territorial and having colorful scales.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.hagfi: A primitive eel-like scavenger, capable of producing large amounts of slime when threatened.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.herri: A small baitfish known for forming large schools.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.john_: A predatory saltwater fish recognized by the large dark spot on its side and highly protrusible jaws.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.lionf: A predatory reef fish with venomous spines, considered invasive in some parts of the world.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.macke: A small baitfish known for forming large schools.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.mahi: An open-water predatory fish, known for its bright colors.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.moray: A snake-like predatory fish that hides in crevices and caves on the coral reef.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.needl: A slender predatory fish with a long beak filled with sharp teeth, often found near the water's surface.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.oarfi: A long deep-sea fish that often appears before earthquakes, thought to be the inspiration behind sea serpents.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.ocean: The largest bony fish in the world, known for its indifference to pain.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.opah: A large open-ocean fish, notable for being one of the few warm-blooded fish in the world.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.parro: An important reef fish, known for its parrot-like beak, as well as its ability to eat corals and produce sand.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.pearl: A small fish that lives inside sea cucumbers.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.piran: A small freshwater fish known for its sharp teeth and voracious appetite.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.pleco: An armored freshwater catfish that feeds on algae and uses its sucker-like mouth to cling to surfaces.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.ratfi: A deep-sea relative of sharks, known for its large eyes, long tail, and unusual appearance.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.rockf: A saltwater fish, known for its large eyes and its tendency to hide among rocks.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.sea_b: A predatory saltwater fish, often used as a food source and known for its delicious flavor.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.seaho: A small reef fish that swims upright, known for its curled tail and the male's ability to carry eggs.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.sheep: A large fish that lives in kelp forests, eating sea urchins and helping keep the kelp alive.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.snail: A deep-sea fish with an extremely soft and fragile body
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.squir: A nocturnal reef fish known for its large eyes and sharp spine on its underside
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.sting: A large circular fish that swims along the seafloor, known for having a venomous spine on the end of its tail.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.stone: A bottom-dwelling fish that mimics the appearance of rocks around it, known for its extremely potent venom.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.sunfi: A common freshwater fish known for its rounded body and willingness to bite almost anything.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.surge: A reef fish, named after sharp protrusions on either side of its tail.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.tetra: A small freshwater fish, known for its bright colors and schooling behaviour.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.tiger: A small freshwater fish, known for its striped pattern and schooling behaviour.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.treva: A schooling fish that prefers to follow large animals around.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.trigg: A large reef fish, known for its sharp teeth and aggressive behaviour, named after a sharp spine protruding out of its back.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.trout: A freshwater fish commonly found in rivers and lakes, valued for its speed and ability to swim upstream.
journal.description.hybrid_aquatic.tuna: An open-water predatory fish that never stops swimming.
